title: Flow-rate Commitment and Throttling Remediation Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Draft a customer-facing playbook that codifies Dedicated capacity throughput commitments (tokens/sec and tokens/min guarantees), the error budget construct used to measure degradations, and the contractual remediation (crediting and operational responses) tied to different classes of degradation. The playbook will: (1) define measurement windows and percentile SLOs for throughput and tail latency; (2) define error budget burn calculations specific to reserved pools and multi-az failover; (3) provide templated contract language and notice windows; (4) outline the autoscaling and throttling interlock behavior and customer-visible outcomes; (5) include runbooks for on-call and customer success for remediation crediting and communication. This ticket focuses on the product & legal wording, operational triggers, and example computations. Engineering tickets will implement telemetry hooks and autoscale interlocks referenced below.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Document contains clear definitions for Primary Commitment (guaranteed tokens/min), Degradation Band (partial availability), and Total Outage
A2: Error budget math documented with worked example for 30-day window and sub-window rebalancing
A3: Contract language templates for Notice, Remedy (credit formula), and Escalation provided in plain language and legal-friendly clause variants
A4: Autoscale and throttling policy described with exact trigger thresholds, expected customer-visible effects, and fallback model mapping
A5: Runbook steps for CS and SRE with links to dashboards and PRs are included
A6: Stakeholder sign-off received from Legal, SRE, and Sales Engineering (evidence in comments)
A7: Security review flagged and any KMS/HSM impact noted

monitoring_and_alerting: Primary metrics: reserved_tokens/min (per-customer), 95th and 99th percentile request latency, queue length, drop-rate due to throttling
SLO windowing: rolling 30-day window with daily sub-window checks (1h and 6h) to detect sudden burn spikes
Alert thresholds: first alert when utilization > 110% sustained for 5 minutes, high-priority when 120% sustained for 2 minutes, paging when error budget burn rate > 5x baseline over 1h
Dashboards: customer-facing SLA dashboard for Sales/CS (read-only) and SRE internal incident dashboard with linked traces and pool mapping
Audit logs: record autoscale decisions, model fallbacks, and customer notifications for post-incident crediting calculations
remediation_calculation: Credit = monthly_subscription_fee * (proportional_service_degradation). Where proportional_service_degradation is computed as weighted sum over time of unmet tokens relative to committed tokens. During multi-az failover, weights apply a 0.5 multiplier to transient failover periods < 5 minutes. Credits cap at 100% of the month's dedicated capacity fee. See sample calculation steps for details.
sample_calculation_steps: Step 1: Define committed capacity: C = 60,000 tokens/min (customer contract)
Step 2: For each 1-minute interval i in the 30-day measurement window compute shortfall S_i = max(0, C - served_tokens_i)
Step 3: Compute time-weighted shortfall TWS = sum(S_i) / (C * total_minutes_in_window)
Step 4: Adjust for transient failovers: for contiguous shortfalls < 5 minutes mark as transient and apply 0.5 weight
Step 5: Error budget burned = TWS expressed as percentage. Example: TWS = 0.12 => 12% degradation => Credit = min(0.12,1.0) * monthly_subscription_fee
Step 6: Apply minimum credit floor: if TWS < 0.01, issue no credit but generate internal RCA and customer advisory
contract_clause_variants: Plain-language clause for sales: 'We commit to X tokens/min sustained. If we fail to provide that capacity, we will credit you proportionally as described in the SLA appendix.'

Legal clause (short): 'Vendor guarantees committed throughput measured as tokens per minute. Dedicated capacity degradation will be computed per Section 3 (Measurement). Customer remedies limited to credits as calculated; cap equals total monthly Dedicated Fee.'

Legal clause (detailed): 'Throughput Commitment: Vendor will maintain committed capacity C. Measurement: 30-day rolling window, with per-minute sampling. Remediation: Credits calculated per Appendix A (flow-rate debit model). Exclusions: scheduled maintenance, customer misconfiguration, DDoS, force majeure. Notice: Customer must provide notice within 30 days to claim credit.'
autoscale_and_throttling_policies: Default behavior: Dedicated pool autoscaler will attempt horizontal scale within reserved cluster by up to 20% temporary burst if capacity > 80% and autoscale cooldown satisfied
Burst policy: bursts applied for up to 10 minutes with telemetry tag 'burst=true'; sustained need escalates to contractual notification and potential autoscale DC (reserved-add) negotiation

Throttling interlock: when pool saturation > 115% and no further autoscale possible, system activates per-customer priority queue. Priority tiers control order; best-effort routes to compatible model variants will be attempted before hard throttling
Fallback mapping: map of models ordered by fidelity/cost such that lower-fidelity variants are used automatically for non-critical routes if the customer opts in
Customer-choice opt-outs: customers can choose 'no-fallback' in contract which disables automatic fidelity fallback and instead triggers immediate credit computation
operational_responses: Immediate: emit SLA degradation event, notify oncall SRE and CS lead, mark customer pool as 'degraded' in console
Triage (0-30m): SRE evaluates autoscale eligibility, applies safe manual scale if available, and determines if degradation is due to localized kernel scheduling or model-level stall
Mitigate (30m-2h): Attempt fallbacks (model variant routing), clear transient hot-keys via cache invalidation, engage infra for node replacement if hardware suspected
Communicate (within 60m): CS issues hold-notice to customer with expected ETA and whether credit will apply per initial measurement
Postmortem (within 72h): RCA, credit computation, legal notification if customer submitted claim, and action items assigned
risks_and_tradeoffs: Aggressive autoscaling reduces perceived failures but increases cost and may change economic guarantees — legal prefers clearer caps on burst and crediting
Allowing automatic fidelity fallbacks minimizes customer-visible outages but can impact output quality — must be opt-in to comply with enterprise data fidelity requirements
Short measurement windows detect regressions quickly but increase noise in credit computations; hybrid windowing (30-day rolling + 6h sub-windows) is adopted to balance sensitivity and fairness

Credit formula complexity: more precise models (minute-level weighting, AZ multipliers) are fairer but harder to audit; we will provide both an executive summary and a full appendix with worked examples
